explanations: observe() records each value in exactly one slot, the first bucket whose bound it fits under. snapshot() then reports those per-slot counts as the bucket counts. The Bucket contract (and Prometheus) expects cumulative counts: le=100 must include everything at or below 100ms, not only values between 50 and 100. Because most bids land in the 10ms bucket, the le=100 bucket looks nearly empty, so fractionWithin reports the SLO as breached, and histogram_quantile gets non-monotonic buckets with +Inf != _count. Keeping a running total in snapshot() makes each bucket count every observation at or below its bound.
